subject: humanities
passage: Because the alluvial plains of Bengal offer little building stone, the temple builders of seventeenth-century Bishnupur worked largely in brick, covering their walls with thousands of carved terracotta panels. Scholars once described this choice as a ______ one, forced on artisans by the scarcity of better materials. Yet the panels, crowded with scenes from the epics and from daily life, display such fluency with fired clay that the material seems not merely tolerated but embraced, its softness before firing permitting a density of detail that stone would have resisted.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

explanation.why: The phrase right after the blank, "forced on artisans by the scarcity of better materials," gives the older view: builders used brick only because they had to. The next sentence answers that view by saying the material was "not merely tolerated." The blank must mean "made unwillingly," which is "reluctant."
explanation.A: Incorrect. A deliberate choice is made freely and on purpose, but the older view described it as "forced."
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Visionary" praises the choice as bold and imaginative, the opposite of a choice that was "forced" by scarcity.
explanation.C: Correct. A choice "forced on artisans" and only "tolerated" is a reluctant one, made unwillingly.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text discusses why builders used brick, not any ritual role of the material.
